description:
Otis (12), Sam (12), Harrison (9) and their dads Tom Torkar and Matt Osbond.

Otis, Sam and Harrison are MInecraft fans and have started their coding journeys.

Mat is a games developer by profession. 

Tom  is a lawyer and is not techy at all but is doing his best
summary: The team were briefed to create a junior astranaut mission trainer.  The team chose mars as a location as it captures the imagination and is "the next frontier".  Youth-targetted STEM content can either be too complex or over-simplify - in each case losing the child's attention.  The mission aim is to turn a game that millions of children already play into a hands-on mission experience enabling them to explore and play. The team created a Minecraft world in which player can explore a Mars environment and interact with challenges based on radiation, power generation, food production.  The game will model radiation spikes (e.g. from solar flares) and dust-storms.
details:
The solution to the challenge is an interactive game based in a Minecraft workd. The player can explore a Mars environment in first-player mode and interact with features (rovers/bases), build and survive in a harsh environment.

Minecraft is a familiar game which is already interactive. However, it is generally used to build and play in imaginary worlds. The aim was to introduce a Mars environment modelled on real Nasa data to introduce challenges that an Astronaut may encounter and allow players to interact with the world and gain an understanding of the environment and the challenges.

The game includes the following features:

- A Mars world based on real-life topography imagery captured by the Curiosity rover

- Three bases that illustrate the challenges that would be faced y a mission - food production; power generation; radiation decontamination. These bases were designed by Samuel, Otis and Harrison.

- Gameplay mechanics that illustrate the elevated impact of radiation on the Mars surface due to the thin atmospher. The mechanic uses real radiation data and converts this into a mechanic where radiation levels accumulate and the astronaut must seek shelter if increases to a dangerous level and ultimately decontaminate at base.

- Gameplay mechanics that illustrate the impact of dust storms on power generation. Photo-voltaic panels must be cleaned.

The team used the following tools:

- Minecraft - to create the radiation decontamination unit and the power generation plant (and a rocket)

- Unreal Engine to create game rules/mechanics

- TinkerCad to create the 3D shapes from scratch, including a Dome, rover, downed satellite, seed tray, solar panels

- CreativeMode to create mods for Minecraft (mars rover and astronaut player)
